title: Table 1. Primary sample and fixed-window sensitivity accounting
note: The primary endpoint accepts qualifying post-anchor sanctions up to 8 May 2026 and requires at least 1,095 days of follow-up. The separate sensitivity restricts qualifying events to the first 1,095 days. Eligible rows and nulls are unchanged; 135 training and 15 validation positives become zeros, while all 20 test positives remain positive. Deferred 2023–2024 rows remain null, including known sanctions. Source: frozen label counts and fixed1095_counts.csv.

title: Table 2A. Matched-input M11 results: feature-only learners and graph references
note: All rows use M11 company inputs and the same 8,435 test observations, including 20 positives. GNNs use the reverse-message graph reference. Means and sample SDs describe five fixed fits; they are not confidence intervals. MLP and GNN losses are positively weighted; the four tabular learners are unweighted. F1 uses a validation-selected threshold; P@5% reviews 422 rows; R@10FPR is a test-ROC summary. L1/L2 logistic and XGBoost have exactly zero recorded across-seed SD. Table 4A supplies direct crossed comparisons; fixed-fit intervals are in Supplement S3/S8a.

title: Table 2B. Retrospective source-status scores (no fitted model)
rows: Any selected source missing after filtering
note: Validation N = 7,309 / 40 positives; test N = 8,435 / 20 positives. The first three scores use source-selection counts; the fourth flags any nonfinite value among 87 final as-of financial columns before learner preprocessing. AUC and step-weighted AP are exact two-bin calculations, not trained baselines or estimates of causal model dependence. Source absence and predictor nonfiniteness are distinct. No confidence intervals are inferred from the counts. Sources: Supplement S9d and the aggregate source_mask_counts.csv.

title: Table 2C. Primary M11 fixed-prediction subset diagnostics
rows: D: no detected earlier document match
B: S + raw fin_ binding screen
note: Cells give five-fit mean AUC / mean hits at the stated budget. D and O retain all 8,415 negatives; O AUC is derived per seed as (20×full−7×D)/13. O MLP/RF hits equal full-test hits because every D hit count is zero; “—” denotes an uncomputed GNN complement yield. S/B filter both classes and J applies D’s positive rule within S. The populations are descriptive screens, not historically clean or independently new cases. No random-composition reference or subset interval is reported. J has two positives, one with unresolved raw fin_ binding. Full metrics and tie details are in S12–S14.

title: Table 3. Primary feature expansion within five non-graph learners
note: Differences are richer minus leaner at fixed primary settings, calculated from unrounded means. This panel is descriptive. Original fixed-fit paired intervals are preserved in Supplement Table S3b and the aggregate source; three of five M11−M5 intervals include zero. Stored-message GNN increments in S3 do not evaluate reverse-message feature expansion. Table 5B separately gives crossed financial-reconstruction contrasts.

title: Table 4A. Primary M11 paired comparisons: crossed company-and-seed uncertainty
note: Reference means: weighted MLP 0.8319; unweighted RF 0.8639. GNN references use reverse messages; the last four rows compare these references with the post-hoc stored-message ablation. Intervals use 2,000 shared company-cluster draws crossed with matched seed labels (4,531 companies; 8,435 observations; 20 positives). They omit case/network blocks, new training data and post-hoc selection and are marginal and unadjusted. GraphSAGE reverse−stored has lower endpoint approximately +0.0000027, not a robust positive margin. The fixed-fit scheme is in Supplement S11. Differences use unrounded means.

title: Table 4B. Findings, evidence and limits
rows: No consistent evidence of GNN superiority at matched M11 inputs; GCN/GraphSAGE gaps are unresolved and GAT/RGCN are lower than MLP.
Fixed models, weighting and one full test; neither equivalence nor architecture-wide inferiority.
Richer inputs raise mean AUC within five feature-only learners.
Descriptive configuration-specific increments, not validated leakage-free disclosure signals.
Indicator-only and historical-graph diagnostics expose different kinds of information.
No universal bound on structural signal; historical-label scores differ from annual GNN inputs.
MLP/RF budgeted hits are document-matched; financial-record flags discriminate outcomes.
Observed source and outcome composition, not causal attribution or new-case validation.
Omitting reverse records lowers GCN AUC in the post-hoc ablation.
An implementation diagnostic changing accessibility and normalization, not the main learner-ranking result.

title: Table 5A. Temporal sensitivity results and paired changes from primary references
note: Five fits per condition; the same 8,435 test labels and 20 positives. Changes are sensitivity minus corresponding primary, with reverse-message references for GCN/GraphSAGE. Intervals use 2,000 crossed company-and-matched-seed draws and omit case/network dependence and new training-data variation. Financial reconstruction changes only 87 fields under the available snapshot. Fixed-window fits retain original features and 119/25 training/validation positives, neural weight 201.5714 and reselected checkpoints/thresholds. Families are separate. Differences use unrounded means.

title: Table 5B. Within-family paired contrasts on the full test
note: Same crossed scheme as Table 5A. MLP is positively weighted; RF is unweighted. Intervals describe these fitted pipelines and test rows, not clean-input, new-case or architecture-wide effects. Both financial M11−M5 AUC intervals contain zero despite positive differences in every seed. Supplement S13 preserves all 16 contrasts, both interval schemes and five metrics.
